transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um, I guess I'm here because of some things going on at work? I drive for a living, and... well, I hope it's okay to talk about this, I really don't want to sound like a complainer or a bad employee. It's just that dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system. And I keep hearing these little comments on the radio about it. 

When I try to ask about it, people say it’s just normal oversight, and I always try to follow the rules, so maybe I'm just overthinking it? Does that sound like normal management stuff to you? It's just... even if it is, I can tell certain other drivers are reporting on me, and I just don't want anyone to think I'm doing a bad job.
When you hear those comments on the radio, do they seem to be directed specifically at you?

Um... yes. I really hope I don't sound paranoid or anything, I know that's probably a bad trait for an employee. But... yeah, they do. 

It's like, the computer system will track a route change I make, and then almost right away there's one of those little comments on the radio. And like I said, I know dispatch says it's just normal oversight, and I really do try to just put my head down and do a good job, but... I can just tell that certain other drivers are using it to report on me. 

I'm sorry, does that make sense? I really try to be easy to work with and follow all the rules, I just... I don't know why they'd be focusing on me like that, and I don't want you to think I'm just making things up.
Have you heard voices when no one was actually speaking to you?

Oh, um... no. No, I don't think so. I mean, the things on the radio are real, like the actual radio in the cab. But just... like, voices out of nowhere? No, I haven't had anything like that. 

I know that's probably a really important question for you to ask, and I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. But no, I haven't heard anything when no one is there. That would mean I was really losing it, right? And I promise, I'm just trying to figure out the work stuff. I really hope I'm being helpful.
Do you believe for certain that your coworkers are intentionally monitoring and reporting on you?

Um, well... I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm accusing anyone of being malicious or anything. I know everybody's just trying to do their jobs, and I really respect that. But... yes, I do. 

I just... I know dispatch says it's normal oversight, but the way the computer system tracks my route changes, and then those little comments on the radio happen right after... it just feels too connected to be a coincidence. And I can just tell that certain drivers are definitely reporting on me. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds like I'm not a team player or that I'm being difficult. I really don't want to be that kind of person. I just want to do my job well and make sure everyone is happy with my work. Does it make sense why I'd feel a little... unsettled by all of that? I hope I'm not overreacting.
Is it possible you might be mistaken about your coworkers intentionally monitoring and reporting on you?

Um... I guess... I mean, I want to say yes, because I know that's probably what I should say, right? I really don't want to seem stubborn or like I can't take feedback. But... I don't know, it's just so hard to explain. 

I know compliance and dispatch say it's just normal oversight, and maybe I am just being too sensitive... but the way they track my route changes through the computer system, and then those comments on the radio... it's just so specific. I can just tell that certain drivers are reporting on me. 

I'm really sorry, I know that probably sounds terrible and defensive. I promise I'm usually very open to being wrong. I just... I can't shake the feeling that it's actually happening. Is it okay that I feel that way? I really hope you don't think I'm a difficult person.
How long have you been feeling that your coworkers are intentionally monitoring and reporting on you?

Um, well... I mean, I really don't want to sound like I've been holding onto this for a long time or letting it affect my work, because I always try to do my best. But... I'd say it's been about two months now. 

Like, the tracking with the computer system and the comments on the radio... it's just felt really clear to me for the past two months. I tried to ignore it at first, I really did, because I know I should just focus on driving and being a good employee. But it's just been pretty consistent since then. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I've been, you know, paranoid or anything for all that time. I just wanted to be honest with you. Does two months sound like a normal amount of time to notice something like that? I really hope I'm giving you the right information.
Do you ever feel that other people can read your thoughts?

Oh, um... no. No, definitely not. I really hope I didn't say anything earlier that made you think I was... you know, losing touch completely. I know the thing about the dispatch and the radios sounds a little intense, and I'm so sorry if it gave the wrong impression. 

But my thoughts are definitely just my own. I've never felt like anyone could read them or hear them or anything like that. I keep my personal thoughts to myself, just like a professional should. 

Is... is it a good sign that I don't feel that way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need, and I really hope you don't think my mind is playing tricks on me.
Aside from the situation with your coworkers, have you noticed yourself becoming less interested in people or activities you usually care about?

Um... well, I really try to stay active and be a good friend, I promise I do. I don't want you to think I'm just lazy or giving up on things. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, I have been a little less involved lately. 

Like, I used to love singing with my choir, and I'd always have the softball team over to my place... but lately, I just haven't really felt like doing any of that. I've been skipping it. And... um, most days after my shift, I just kind of sit at the kitchen table. I'll have my planner open and everything, like I'm going to be productive, but I just... I can't seem to make myself start dinner, or make any phone calls, or do much of anything else. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds awful, like I'm just wasting time. I really want to be doing those things, I just feel kind of... empty, I guess? Is it normal to feel that way when you're stressed out from work? I hope you don't think I'm just letting my life fall apart.
Have you been feeling depressed?

Um... no, not depressed. I mean, I know sitting at the table and not doing my hobbies sounds a lot like depression, and I'm really sorry if I made it seem that way. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself or crying all the time, because I'm definitely not. 

I'm not sad or down, really. It's more just... a lack of energy to get things started, you know? Like I said, I just feel kind of blank or empty, but not sad. I still want to be a happy, productive person. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining the difference clearly. I just don't want to give you the wrong idea and have you think I'm dealing with something I'm not. I'm trying really hard to give you accurate answers.
Have you been having trouble keeping up with your work or basic daily tasks like bathing, dressing, or eating?

Um... well, I really try to keep on top of things, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just letting everything go. I still make sure I'm showered and dressed nicely every day, because I know how important it is to look professional. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, some of the other things have been a little harder lately. At work, I've... well, I've fallen a little behind on my route reports. And I guess some of my instructions over the radio have been a bit confusing for the drivers. They've complained a couple of times, which I feel terrible about. I really always try to do my best for them.

And at home... well, my husband has been so sweet, he's kind of had to take over making dinner and handling the phone calls and just... figuring out our daily plans. I just haven't been keeping up with it the way I usually do. 

I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds like I'm not trying hard enough. I really don't want to be a burden on my husband or my coworkers. Is it okay that I'm struggling with this a little bit right now? I just hope you don't think I'm a failure or anything. I really am trying.
Have you had times when your thoughts or speech felt jumbled or hard to organize?

Um... well, I don't think my thoughts are jumbled, exactly. I really try to be clear when I talk to people. I don't want you to think I'm losing my mind or anything like that. 

But... I guess there are some things I do at work that might seem a little... odd to other people? I'm almost embarrassed to mention it. Like, sometimes I'll get kind of stuck rearranging the magnets and the route slips on the board. I have to put them in a very specific pattern. And... um, when the drivers call in, sometimes I find myself repeating their last few words back to them before I answer. 

I know it probably sounds strange, and I've noticed people looking at me like I'm just being difficult or weird. I really, really don't mean to be! I'm just trying so hard to keep the whole board from going wrong, you know? It feels like if I don't do those things, everything will get messed up. 

I'm sorry, I hope that doesn't make me sound completely crazy. Is it okay that I do that to help me stay organized? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job for everyone.
For how long altogether have these changes been going on for you?

Um... well, it hasn't been forever, I promise. I don't want you to think this is just how I am all the time. I've always been a really hard worker. 

I guess... if I really think about it, it's been building up for about eight months now? It started right around the time they put me in the temporary dispatch lead role at work. It was a lot of new responsibility all at once, and I just wanted to do such a good job for them, you know? I really wanted to prove that they made the right choice in picking me. 

So maybe the stress of wanting to be perfect just sort of... caught up with me a little bit? I'm sorry, I know eight months sounds like a long time to let things slide. I really thought I could just push through it and get back to normal on my own. I hope you don't think I've been irresponsible for waiting this long to talk about it. Does that timeline make sense with what I've been telling you?

Um... well, I don't think my thoughts are jumbled, exactly. I really try to be clear when I talk to people. I don't want you to think I'm losing my mind or anything like that. 

But... I guess there are some things I do at work that might seem a little... odd to other people? I'm almost embarrassed to mention it. Like, sometimes I'll get kind of stuck rearranging the magnets and the route slips on the board. I have to put them in a very specific pattern. And... um, when the drivers call in, sometimes I find myself repeating their last few words back to them before I answer. 

I know it probably sounds strange, and I've noticed people looking at me like I'm just being difficult or weird. I really, really don't mean to be! I'm just trying so hard to keep the whole board from going wrong, you know? It feels like if I don't do those things, everything will get messed up. 

I'm sorry, I hope that doesn't make me sound completely crazy. Is it okay that I do that to help me stay organized? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job for everyone.

Um... well, it hasn't been forever, I promise. I don't want you to think this is just how I am all the time. I've always been a really hard worker. 

I guess... if I really think about it, it's been building up for about eight months now? It started right around the time they put me in the temporary dispatch lead role at work. It was a lot of new responsibility all at once, and I just wanted to do such a good job for them, you know? I really wanted to prove that they made the right choice in picking me. 

So maybe the stress of wanting to be perfect just sort of... caught up with me a little bit? I'm sorry, I know eight months sounds like a long time to let things slide. I really thought I could just push through it and get back to normal on my own. I hope you don't think I've been irresponsible for waiting this long to talk about it. Does that timeline make sense with what I've been telling you?
